title: Lua-to-YAML converter emits numeric `time`, breaking the downstream string parser
outcome_detail: Ticket 06 / PR #677 — the converter emitted a numeric `time`, and TimeExpressionParser.parse starts with expression.strip(), so a number raised AttributeError downstream. The shipped versions.yaml confirms the intended shape is a string ('sunrise', '08:30'), so seconds since midnight are now formatted HH:MM. Guarded with `is not None` rather than truthiness: midnight is 0 and would have been dropped silently. 5 tests, one of which feeds the emitted value straight into the consumer.

title: `_extract_list` escape handling ignores string state and doubled backslashes
outcome_detail: Confirmed, and it empties the list rather than truncating it. `_extract_list` tested `content[i - 1] == chr(92)` regardless of string state, where `_extract_table` ten lines above uses an `escape_next` flag honoured only inside a string. So an ordinary Windows path in a Lua string left the closing quote looking escaped, the string never closed, and no brace after it was counted — measured: zero tables returned instead of two. Aligned with `_extract_table`. 6 tests.

title: Visibility regex matches unrelated 4-digit METAR tokens
outcome_detail: Confirmed, and the mechanism is worse than the title suggests: the visibility branch has no break, so the *last* four-digit group won. Everything from TEMPO, BECMG, PROB or RMK onwards is a forecast or free text, not the current observation, so a report observed at 9999 and ending in 'TEMPO 3000' was flown at 3000 m. The parser now stops at those words and takes the first prevailing visibility only. 5 tests. An `i > 0` guard I added first against a numeric station identifier was removed: ICAO codes are alphabetic, so it protected nothing and broke two existing tests that parse a bare token.

commits: 7d368dd5 feat(build): disable kneeboard generation while keeping radio presets (FEAT-PRESETS-KNEEBOARD-TOGGLE) (#564)
outcome_detail: Confirmed, and 10 occurrences across 8 files rather than the one reported. `exit()` is installed by the site module, not part of the language: absent under `python -S` and not guaranteed in the PyInstaller exe this project ships. `typer.Exit` was already the idiom in the same directory (ask.py, capture_map.py, prepare.py), so these were leftovers. Replacing them found dead code as a bonus: prepare.py called exit(1) after logger.error, which raises typer.Abort by default -- the line was unreachable. A gate now parses commands/ with ast; written as a regex first, it missed the two `exit(1)` forms that were not alone on their line, which is how the count went from 8 to 10.

title: dictionaryNormalizer executes an untrusted dictionary file via loadfile/setfenv
outcome_detail: The sandbox the finding overlooks is right there: loadTable does setfenv(file, table) with table = {}, so the loaded dictionary runs with an empty environment and reaches no global at all -- no os, no io, no require, not even setmetatable. Arbitrary code execution is not available. A hostile file can still spin or allocate, but this is a developer tool run by hand on one's own files, so that is a denial of service against oneself.

Remote marker command runs stored Lua via mist.utils.dostring gated by shared static password
outcome_detail: Inherited from VMR-040 and now materially reduced by it: the remote Lua execution is gated on the ADMIN tier, and a mission that declares its own hashes no longer accepts the public password at any tier. What remains -- that an authenticated admin can run arbitrary Lua -- is the feature, not a defect: it is how a server operator drives their own server. Any further hardening belongs to REVIEW-SECURITY-LAYER with the authorization layer's own tests, not to a LOW sweep.

title: Empty monitoredCommands makes the remote marker command path dead/unreachable
Passwords hashed with unsalted single-round SHA-1; shared secrets committed in source
outcome_detail: David's call, taken on 2026-08-10, and it dissolved the dilemma I had framed. The choice was not between breaking every server and merely documenting: `password_MM` has always been REPLACED by the generator (`veafSecurity.password_MM = {}` before the adds) while `password_L1` was only extended -- three lines apart. So a mission declaring its own hashes widened the accepted set instead of closing it, and the public hash kept opening it. Declaring password_hashes now clears L0/L1/L9 first. L0 too, deliberately: checkPassword_L1 accepts L1 OR L0, so leaving the shipped L0 hash would have made the change decorative. Consequence to know: on a mission that declares its own hashes, nothing grants ADMIN by password any more -- ADMIN comes from the pilot's level in veaf-pilots.txt. Missions that declare nothing keep the shipped defaults, so no silent change. 4 tests. The unsalted SHA-1 itself is untouched: a known password is known whatever the digest, and the fix that matters is being able to turn it off.

title: getMarkerSecurityLevel conflates markId and username, weakening marker author trust
outcome_detail: Confirmed as a design defect, and the code says so itself: 'markId may actually be the username if called from veafRemote - yes I know it's ugly'. Not exploitable in practice -- the username fallback only fires when no mark panel carries the id, and it would then have to collide with a registered remote user's name, which are pilot names rather than integers. The fix is a signature split in the authorization layer, which belongs with REVIEW-SECURITY-LAYER and its tests rather than in a LOW sweep touching ten unrelated files.

title: Remote fog command indexes veafWeather with attacker-supplied key without whitelisting
outcome_detail: Not exploitable as reported. The key is player-supplied but goes through :upper(), and every all-caps key on veafWeather is a FOG_* preset -- measured across the file, there is no other. So the missing whitelist reaches nothing but fog objects. The fragility underneath was real and is removed: the command now checks the contract setAndActivateFog is about to use, so the first all-caps constant that is not a fog object cannot turn a pilot's request into a Lua error. 3 tests.

title: deployWaves/tickActive dereference triggerZone/zoneCenter without full nil handling
outcome_detail: Confirmed, and reachable precisely because of a deliberate leniency. `setTriggerZone` stores the name before checking the zone, and when a centre is already configured it only warns — so `deployWaves` saw a `triggerZoneName`, got nil from `veaf.getTriggerZone` and indexed it: every wave of such a zone raised. Now asks for the zone and then decides, the same shape as `AirWaveZone:check()` two hundred lines above, with an explicit refusal when neither is usable. 3 tests. Noted in passing, not fixed: `setTriggerZone` writes a vec2 into `zoneCenter` while the documented contract of `setZoneCenter` is a vec3 — harmless today because the vec2 only exists when the trigger zone does.

The dead branch also read a global `parameters` rather than `_parameters`, which is why nothing ever surfaced. 4 tests. The duration is not bounded, which is unchanged: the radio menu already offers 45 and 90 minutes.

title: Unreachable armorBias branch: _actualDefense > 5 never true after clamp
outcome_detail: The branch is reachable, so the finding's premise is wrong. `if _actualDefense > 5 then _actualDefense = 6 end` is not a clamp to 5 — it promotes to 6, which is what makes the `> 5` branch below fire (defense 5 plus a dice roll above 80). The two tiers spawn different units (Roland ADS / Gepard against the level-5 set), so this is a working 'super' tier, not dead code. What remains is the finding's second half — that `_addDefenseForGroups` and `generateAirDefenseGroup` disagree on the ceiling — and removing tier 6 would change mission balance, which is David's call, not a sweep's.

commits: 3c09574f feat(assist): guided checklists from YAML, with F-16C engine start as first client (#649)

The locale worry that argued for hand-formatting was tested and does not reproduce: `%.6f` keeps the decimal point even after `os.setlocale("French_France.1252")`. 4 tests.

title: Sanctuary event filter operator-precedence bug lets non-tracked BIRTH/DEAD events register
outcome_detail: Confirmed, and the finding's remedy would have been a regression. `A or B and C and D` parses as `A or (B and C and D)`, so PLAYER_ENTER_UNIT/LEAVE_UNIT skipped the name check and registered under the key `""`. But parenthesising as `(A or B) and C and D`, as proposed, would require the `humanUnits` lookup on PLAYER_ENTER_UNIT — and that table is filled once at initialize() from `mist.DBs.humansByName`, so a **dynamic slot** is not in it and Sanctuary would stop following those players entirely. Proved by applying the proposed remedy and watching the dynamic-slot test fail. The two branches differ: ENTER/LEAVE is a human by definition and needs only a name; BIRTH/DEAD fires for AI too and does need the lookup. 9 tests.

title: authenticate() silently ignores malformed timeout and mis-parses embedded digits
outcome_detail: Confirmed, and it is a crash rather than a silent ignore. `-auth login <duration>` reaches `authenticate` as text a pilot typed, and the guard `not actualMinutes:match("%d+")` was unanchored: "abc5" passed it and `actualMinutes * 60` then raised (measured in Lua 5.1). "-5" passed too and scheduled the logout in the past, so the mission unlocked and relocked without a word. Now converted with `tonumber` and refused when nil or <= 0, with a warning. 7 tests.

The four legs are called with 0.3, 0.5, 0.63 and 0.63, so every CAP spawned without an explicit speed flew its entire route at Mach 0.3 -- visible in game as sluggish patrols. `mach or 0.3` keeps the old value as a fallback for a caller that passes nothing.

The reported off-by-one does NOT apply: `numberSpawned` is pre-incremented (set to 1 before the first spawn), so `> maximumAmount` already refuses the 9th AFAC — `>=` would have capped missions at 7. Both limits are now pinned by tests.

title: convertLaserToFreq accepts codes outside the valid DCS laser range in the low digits

Found on the way: an existing test asserted 1500 produced a frequency, and both GUIDE pages documented the keyword as `code` (which is the TACAN channel) instead of `laser`. 11 tests.

title: getAtis new-ATIS detection triggers on any lower date component, not strict chronology
outcome_detail: Disproved by enumeration, not by reading. Under a monotonic clock the shipped per-component `or` chain is exactly equivalent to a lexicographic (year, month, day, hour) comparison: 26 304 hour blocks over three years, 345 963 360 ordered pairs, **zero divergence**. The control — the same comparison with the clock allowed to run backwards — does diverge, so the probe is not hollow. `timer.getAbsTime()` never runs backwards, so there is nothing to fix.
